title: Problem 1
statement_text: Find the minimal constant $\widehat{\rho}\in[0,1]$ such that each spectrally symmetric graph satisfies $\frac{2|E(G)|}{|V(G)|^{2}}\leq\widehat{\rho}$.
context_text: For a digraph $D$ with $a(i,j)$ arcs from $i$ to $j$, the Hermitian adjacency matrix of the second kind is $H(D)=H_{\pi/3}(D)$ with entries $H_{i,j}=e^{i\pi/3}a(i,j)+e^{-i\pi/3}a(j,i)$. A digraph is spectrally symmetric if the spectrum of $H(D)$ is symmetric about $0$, and an undirected graph is spectrally symmetric if it has at least one spectrally symmetric orientation (an assignment of a direction to each edge). Bipartite graphs are spectrally symmetric, but the converse fails (e.g. an orientation of $K_5-E(K_3)$). For undirected adjacency spectra, symmetry forces bipartiteness and hence at most $n^2/4$ edges (Mantel), i.e. density $2|E|/|V|^2\le\frac12$; the problem asks for the analogous density threshold for spectrally symmetric orientations. The authors prove the upper bound $\widehat{\rho}\le\frac{10}{11}$ (a spectral analogue of Mantel's theorem for digraphs; blow-ups of a spectrally symmetric digraph remain spectrally symmetric with the same limit density). An earlier arXiv version had the lower bound $\frac{13}{18}$ from a $6$-vertex example; in the final version, after Seamons found a spectrally symmetric orientation of $K_{11}-3K_2$ (giving $\frac{104}{121}$), the authors give one of $K_{12}-4K_2$, so that $\frac{31}{36}\le\widehat{\rho}\le\frac{10}{11}$. The exact value remains open.
